correctness.rationale: The coordinate model is sign-symmetric, with moments of degree 2 equal to 1/3 on the coordinate squares. The pure and mixed fourth moments are 1/5 and 1/15, using (1+φ²)^2=5φ²; the even moments and sign cancellations establish the full sampler isometry on products of harmonics through degree two. The probability-normalized addition kernel gives the complement Q_{xx}=1/4, Q_{x,−x}=−1/4 and Q_{xy}=−(x·y)/4 for other pairs. Subtracting the erased Gram from the identity gives 9−r unit domain eigenvalues and the eigenvalues of Q_{E,E}, including zeros. An antipodal triple reduces to a 2-by-2 block with diagonal 2,1 and off-diagonal magnitude √2/√5 before dividing by 4; nonantipodal triples switch to constant signed off-diagonal −c or +c, where c=1/√5. Opposite pairs number six, opposite triples 60; product sign on three axes is preserved by antipodal lifts, and the 20 triangular faces occur as ten opposite pairs, one for each positive axis triple. The other ten axis triples are negative. This proves the 80/80 split, the worst admissible eigenvalue (1−2c)/4 and thus the stated condition number. Four or more removed samples force a kernel by dimension. Running python3 /workspace/reproductions/icosa.py constructed 4Q by Galois conjugation of the vertex Gram and independently verified the exact characteristic polynomials for all 12 singles, 66 pairs and 220 triples, with their counts. The normalization is fixed weights, not a renormalized retained sampler.
